Its divergence has strictly negative area integral even at the endpoint, excluding periodic and homoclinic recurrence. A backwards stable branch with bounded radius would yield an alpha-limit at a forbidden equilibrium or have divergent height forcing outward radial growth, so both cross sqrt(5). Thereafter quintic radial growth causes finite-time backward blow-up, while integrable squared radius makes z and theta converge. Integrating the radial inverse fourth power and linear z/theta equations gives all three coefficients, including the e-dependent angular one. Proper-line separation establishes the full two-basin classification. SymPy identities and eight finite integrations replay from the packaged verifier, but are not substituted for analytical proof.
